capabilities.title: Durable local conversation and built-in skill registry
capabilities.contract: Each Article has one persisted greeting and a durable local conversation for built-in Skills. Every persisted Author message is a checkpoint for atomically rejecting that request and the later active conversation. A linked checkpoint restores Article content by appending an immutable restore Revision; displaced Revisions stay available. Draft preservation is the default and explicit discard remains available. Quick Actions show built-in Skill starters; slash filtering refreshes and includes matching Author Skills, while Send remains the sole request trigger. The live Assistant uses a six-step bounded catalog-tool loop with catalog-owned validation, Skill discovery, conversation history, stale-Revision rejection, and one primary generated artifact. It can inspect Article context, Revisions, artifacts, publishing guidance, and Style Corpus state, and reject one explicitly identified prepared translation Proposal without changing Article history. A separate structured intent check using the configured Text Generation Model accepts explicit exact action requests in the Author's language and fails closed before server validation; orchestrating model tool calls and general Article conversation cannot authorize mutation. Selection-scoped requests remain limited to their selected text and cannot call whole-Article capabilities. Revision-bound requests retain their selected or resolved Skill, completed messages, execution metadata, and review artifacts. Fact Check shows Article-ordered claims as pending, checking, or checked, including reused unchanged supported claims. Talking Points prioritizes the active selection, then Author message, then Article. Narrative Draft follows Author direction, develops only the selected source when present, and treats character limits as guidance. Every artifact capability follows the same terminal policy: necessary reads and authorized actions precede generation; identical calls share one execution, conflicting calls fail before a second generation, and the validated artifact finishes orchestration without another model reply. A failed replacement verification leaves a review Proposal available and cannot authorize an automatic edit.
capabilities.persistence: Assistant messages, requests, completed artifacts, and minimal per-capability execution history persist locally. Checkpoint restoration rejects tail artifacts without deleting their audit records and uses an opaque token to detect conversation, Revision, or Draft races. Execution history retains only capability ID, status, request ID, base Revision, and timestamps; Workflow Stage persistence is retired and legacy values remain untouched.

capabilities.title: Streamed responses, progress, cancellation, and error recovery
capabilities.contract: Assistant requests stream typed status, renderer-safe capability activity, and response events. Conversational output reveals completed Markdown blocks without rewriting earlier blocks; review artifacts transition directly from the temporary stream to a short result card with an explicit action to their owning Workspace View, and the current View stays unchanged until the Author follows that action. Completed messages identify a used Skill and expose its localized name through a native title. Streaming follows only when the Author is already near the latest output; scrolling away exposes a return-to-end control, while completion brings the outcome control into view unless focus remains in the Assistant. Failed and cancelled requests expose a Retry action that replays only the local persisted input; an unavailable AI connection also offers Application Settings. Incomplete streams do not modify an Article.
capabilities.persistence: Only valid completed request output becomes local message or review-artifact state. Requests have a service-enforced deadline, defaulting to two minutes and configurable in General Settings. Timeout records a failed request and closes outstanding capability executions, aborts provider work, discards late output, and exposes retry guidance without changing the Article. The deadline also covers replacement verification, edit-intent verification, and Revision descriptions; delivery of a committed completion cannot change its terminal status.

capabilities.title: Model-selected Skills and Author-requested Skill creation
capabilities.contract: An untagged Assistant request uses the configured Assistant model and the discoverable Skill catalog rather than a default editorial workflow. The model may load a relevant Skill and, only for an explicit Author request, create or manage a validated local Markdown Skill through bounded server tools. Revision, restoration, and deletion require the exact Author-requested action and target plus the expected current package hash. Selecting Skill Creator keeps the Article as the chat host without promoting its Draft or using an Article selection as request context. The initial Assistant turn receives no Article body; a later classified editorial capability receives only the context it needs. Creator uncertainty remains conversational. Creation makes a valid Skill available immediately without a separate preview, Install action, or Draft trial. Invalid packages return a specific correction. The selected Creator path changes no Article content, Draft, Proposal, or Revision. Restoring an Assistant chat checkpoint does not change Skills.
capabilities.persistence: Completed creation, revision, or restoration makes the local Skill immediately discoverable and records an immutable file-backed Skill Revision. Deletion removes the live package while retaining history; an explicit Skill Revision restoration can recover it. Incomplete or failed Assistant runs leave no new installed Skill or Skill Revision. Startup recovery reconciles interrupted Skill writes with the durable Assistant request status. Skill Revision history is separate from Article history.

capabilities.title: Thesis-to-narrative composition
capabilities.contract: The server creates a body-only composition Proposal from author-supplied theses, keeping the existing Article title separate; it remains reviewable until acceptance.
capabilities.persistence: Completed proposal artifacts are local and revision-bound.

capabilities.title: Flow revision
capabilities.contract: Flow revision generates a full-body Proposal with the existing Article title kept separate rather than silently editing the Article.
capabilities.persistence: Completed proposal artifacts are local and revision-bound.

capabilities.title: Fact-check request
capabilities.contract: An explicit Fact Check or Assistant request creates advisory findings. Assistant Fact Checks first show claim preparation, then a stable Article-ordered claim list with pending, checking, and checked states; highlighted checkbox rows let the Author deselect or reselect claims until the Assistant finishes, while completed rows are read-only. Deselected claims do not become findings. While a new check runs, the Fact Check View labels earlier completed findings as such and reports the current claim count; it updates after the new run completes. Previously checked claims still stated in the Article remain eligible alongside up to 12 additional claims; exact existing claims are retained even if extraction omits them. Up to three claims are researched and evaluated concurrently. If an Assistant time limit expires or an individual claim fails, completed claim findings are returned as an incomplete Fact Check; unfinished or failed claims are excluded. If no findings complete, the request fails. A fully checked Fact Check survives a timeout or failure in the Assistant's final reply. Exact or conservatively matched rewritten Facts can reuse sourced evidence; changed or uncertain claims are researched again. Accepted decisions follow unchanged Facts, while corrected or removed claims are rechecked if they reappear. A correction request verifies selected unresolved disputed or unverifiable occurrences against the current Revision on the server before generation and creates one reviewable Proposal.
capabilities.persistence: Durable Facts, separate Revision occurrences, findings, citations, checked times, and resolutions are stored locally without changing Article text.

capabilities.title: Style review
capabilities.contract: Style review uses only the current compact, explicitly rebuilt profile plus Article-specific manual rules; its full-body Proposal keeps the existing Article title separate, raw style samples remain local, and review findings retain freshness state with the grounded trait or rule that supports each finding.
capabilities.persistence: Raw style corpus and derived review artifacts stay local.

capabilities.title: Translation request
capabilities.contract: Translation requests prepare a translated Article title and body in separate structured fields; the source Article is never overwritten. Workspace generation confirms selected supported languages and whole-Article scope, then saves a changed Draft once. Unchanged content keeps its source Revision. Each confirmed attempt starts independent request identities, including the same language on an unchanged Revision; Retry retains the failed request's parameters. Batch languages share one source Revision and run at most three requests concurrently. Assistant history displays each explicit translation target beside the Author's Translation chip, including after reload. Each request binds its explicit target language and retains independent completion, failure, and recovery; Cancel stops all active requests and starts no queued languages. Active-Article request guards prevent duplicate starts. Earlier completed results and selection survive fresh request failure or cancellation; completion freshness gates reject changed source output.
capabilities.persistence: Translation review metadata is local and source linkage remains recoverable.

capabilities.title: Summarized diff review, bulk acceptance or rejection, fallback, and stale protection
capabilities.contract: Authors may switch Proposal diffs between side-by-side and stacked layouts, then independently toggle exact-text highlighting in either layout. Highlighting marks changed original text in bright red and changed proposed text in bright green within the existing light paragraph backgrounds. Authors may review non-authoritative Interface-locale summaries, decide every change locally, apply the accepted subset in one Revision, accept a whole Proposal in one Revision, or dismiss stale and zero-change Proposals without Article changes. Zero-change Proposals are labelled Unchanged. Accepted Proposals restore with read-only decisions instead of becoming stale. Fact corrections preserve blank-line formatting. Summary failure does not block review. A stale warning and recovery actions replace decision actions in the review header; preservation warnings remain above patterned diffs in scrolling review content. Labelled change navigation remains reachable outside it and scrolls and focuses the selected change at review start; stale or unreliable Proposals cannot be partially accepted. Whole-Proposal fallback discloses its change count.
capabilities.persistence: Completed Proposal content, summaries with their Interface locale, and the base Revision remain locally recoverable in the Proposal artifact; acceptance creates one immutable Revision whose provenance links the Proposal artifact, and rejection leaves Article history unchanged.

capabilities.title: Explicit request and explicit proposal approval
capabilities.contract: AI operations require an Author request. Ordinary generated text remains separate until explicit acceptance. One eligible conversational reply can be applied by an Author click; opt-in direct mode applies only a separately verified exact edit instruction after valid completion. Stale Revision and Draft conflicts block both paths.
capabilities.persistence: Only Author-clicked or explicitly requested direct edits create attributable immutable Revisions.

capabilities.title: Named multi-provider AI connections
capabilities.contract: A selected model resolves through its active OpenAI, OpenCode Zen, Anthropic, Google Gemini API, xAI Grok, or DeepSeek connection without exposing its credential. Basic text generation may use a configured manual model ID; Style review, Translation, and sourced Fact Check require a supported model capability. Unsupported work is rejected before Article content is sent with guidance to choose a capable model or connection.
capabilities.persistence: Connection metadata and each connection's activation state persist locally; environment credentials remain external and managed credentials remain in the supported operating-system credential store.

capabilities.title: Refreshed model list and purpose-specific model preferences
capabilities.contract: Connection-bound default models and built-in-skill overrides determine editorial requests. A separate optional app model handles Skladno features such as Proposal summaries, titles, and action-intent checks and falls back to the default. Each adapter receives only model options it supports. Structured and sourced operations are capability-gated before the Article is sent.
capabilities.persistence: Connection-bound editorial preferences and the independent app model persist globally; refreshed provider model lists are not persisted.

scenarios.title: Assistant requests stop at their configured deadline
preconditions: A capability or a required completion verification does not finish before the request time limit.
scenarios.event: The default or configured deadline expires.
expected: The provider signal is aborted. Translation and other unfinished operations fail without an artifact. A Fact Check with completed claim findings returns only those findings in a durable run marked incomplete; a fully checked Fact Check remains complete if only the Assistant reply times out.
forbidden: Late provider completion persists additional findings or changes the Article.

scenarios.title: Narrative Draft develops Author-controlled material
preconditions: The author explicitly selects Narrative Draft.
scenarios.event: The author requests a narrative from an Article or selection, optionally with a composer message and publishing-profile limit.
expected: Author direction has priority, an active selection replaces whole Article content as the Article source, and the selected character limit is advisory guidance for the resulting complete Article.
The proposal develops supplied ideas simply unless the Author requests otherwise; the existing Article title remains separate from proposed body text.
forbidden: Inventing unsupported arguments, using unselected Article content, or treating the character hint as an output-token limit.

scenarios.title: Assistant accepts current Skill IDs only
preconditions: An Assistant request names an Editorial operation as its Skill ID.
expected: The operation name is rejected as an unsupported Skill ID.
forbidden: Translating an Editorial operation name into a Skill ID or persisting a new request.

scenarios.title: Talking Points uses the nearest Author input
preconditions: The author explicitly selects Talking Points.
scenarios.event: The author requests theses with or without a composer message.
expected: An Article selection is the primary thesis source when present and the Author message may guide or explicitly extend it; otherwise a non-empty Author message is used, then Article content.
The default output is 3–5 theses, or focused clarifying questions when direction is ambiguous.
forbidden: Using unselected whole Article content when an Article selection is present.

scenarios.title: Assistant request produces a revision-bound proposal
preconditions: The author has an Article and requests a selected-text improvement.
scenarios.event: The Assistant resolves an eligible skill and completes its request.
expected: The request, messages, and revision-bound Proposal artifact are retained locally.
forbidden: Silent changes to the source Article text.

scenarios.title: Author-requested Skills are managed without Article changes
preconditions: A configured Assistant model can use bounded Skill management tools.
scenarios.event: The Author explicitly asks the Assistant to create, revise, restore, or delete an Author Skill.
expected: Creation, revision, and restoration update the live Skill and append immutable Skill Revisions; deletion removes the live package but retains history.
The initial model request receives no Article body, and restoring an Assistant chat checkpoint never changes a Skill.
forbidden: A default Flow workflow, an Article or Draft change, or a Proposal created as part of Skill management.

scenarios.title: Assistant checkpoint restoration preserves Author work atomically
preconditions: An Author message has a linked Revision and later conversation work.
scenarios.event: The Author confirms checkpoint restoration, preserving or explicitly discarding a current Draft.
expected: The selected request and complete later tail become inactive, generated artifacts become non-actionable, and linked Article content becomes current through a new restore Revision.
A preserved Draft becomes an immutable Revision first; later displaced Revisions remain listed and restorable after restart.
forbidden: Partial restoration, hidden or deleted Revisions, stale late provider output, or fallback to conversation-only restoration for a mismatched Revision.

scenarios.title: Assistant streaming preserves completed blocks and hands off review artifacts
preconditions: An Assistant request is streaming in the Assistant timeline.
scenarios.event: The provider sends partial Markdown text, then stages and completes a conversational or review response.
expected: Incomplete text remains hidden, completed blocks retain their rendered identity, and a review response becomes one result card without its full artifact body.
Streaming does not pull a reader who has scrolled upward; completion exposes its outcome control unless focus is within the Assistant.
forbidden: An empty completion frame or duplicate Proposal content beside its review handoff.

scenarios.title: Failed or cancelled Assistant work remains recoverable
preconditions: An Assistant or editorial stream is in progress.
scenarios.event: The stream fails, is incomplete, or is cancelled.
expected: A stable error can be shown and unfinished output is not persisted as valid work.
forbidden: Modifying the Article with incomplete output.

scenarios.title: Composition and flow revision remain proposals
preconditions: The author explicitly requests an editorial operation.
scenarios.event: The server completes a composition or flow-revision operation.
expected: A reviewable Proposal is produced with the source Article unchanged.
forbidden: Applying generated text without author approval.

scenarios.title: Selected Fact corrections require review and a current Revision
preconditions: A current Fact Check has disputed or unverifiable occurrences.
scenarios.event: The Author selects occurrences, reviews the correction Proposal, and accepts or dismisses it.
expected: The server rejects missing, resolved, or stale selections before model invocation; one completed Proposal retains the selected occurrence IDs; accepting the whole Proposal appends a Revision and resolves only its selected occurrences in one transaction.
forbidden: Generation from unverified findings, direct Article changes, resolution on dismissal, or resolution after a Revision conflict.

scenarios.title: Fact and style review preserve Article text
preconditions: The author explicitly requests a fact or style review.
expected: Revision-tied advisory findings and citations are retained.
forbidden: Review output overwriting Article text or sending raw style corpus text.

scenarios.title: Translation retains source independence
preconditions: The author explicitly requests a translation target language.
scenarios.event: The translation operation completes and the author creates its linked Article.
expected: The linked translation retains source metadata and protected spans.

scenarios.title: Paragraph changes retain alignment and independent acceptance
preconditions: A Proposal inserts, deletes, splits, or merges paragraphs.
scenarios.event: The author reviews and accepts selected change groups.
expected: Unchanged nonblank lines anchor change groups; replacements with matching paragraph structure remain independently reviewable; split and merged paragraphs stay grouped.
Applying a group preserves unselected content, Article order, and unchanged protected content.
forbidden: Pairing unrelated paragraphs when their paragraph structure differs.

scenarios.title: Stale proposal remains reviewable but cannot be accepted
preconditions: A Proposal base Revision is no longer current.
expected: The stale warning and recovery actions appear in the review header, acceptance actions are absent, and proposal dismissal remains available.
forbidden: Creating a Revision from a stale Proposal.

scenarios.title: Repeated translation retains source Revision and independent request identities
preconditions: An unchanged Article already has a completed translation.
scenarios.event: The Author confirms another translation, then encounters failure or cancellation.
expected: New request identities use the same source Revision. Earlier results and selection survive failure and cancellation.
forbidden: Synthetic source Revisions or loss of completed results.

scenarios.title: Connection metadata stays distinct from secrets
preconditions: The author configures AI connection metadata.
scenarios.event: The author adds, selects, or removes a connection.
expected: Only environment-variable references and active connection metadata persist.

scenarios.title: Model preferences resolve for new requests
preconditions: A default model, app model, or skill-specific override is configured.
scenarios.event: A new editorial request resolves its model.
expected: The applicable editorial override, app-model preference, or default model is selected.
forbidden: Treating a refreshed provider list as persisted preference data.
